log.text:
The road erupts around you—ferns whipping, boots pounding packed earth, steel flashing in the dim amber light. You came through Cormyr’s King’s Forest to escort a caravan safely along this stretch of road; now the caravan is gone, and three desperate robbers have chosen you as their next prize.

One bandit bursts from the left fern bank, another advances between the trunks to the north, and a third blocks the road with a crossbow leveled at the party. The trees offer cover, but the ambush has already closed around you. What do you do?
We draw steel as they come — where exactly are they, and how close?

The three attackers are already inside sword range: the **Fern-Bank Bandit** is five feet northwest, the **Trunkside Bandit** stands ten feet north, and the **Roadblock Bandit** holds the road five feet west with his crossbow drawn. Elara is ten feet southwest of you, Pip ten feet south; the trees and fern banks break up the open road around you.

Steel clears leather. What do you do?
I charge the nearest one and swing!

pc:pc-1-fighter.backstory: Aldric spent several years guarding caravans along Cormyr’s forest roads. After a former escort job ended in an ambush, he kept the dented buckle from that company and now refuses to let another roadside attack go unanswered.

pc:pc-2-wizard.name: Elara

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.text: Once/day on a short rest, recover spell slots totaling up to half your wizard level (rounded up).

pc:pc-2-wizard.backstory: Elara left a minor magical academy in Suzail to study practical spellcraft beyond lecture halls. She has been seeking situations where careful magic, terrain, and preparation matter more than formal dueling.

pc:pc-3-rogue.name: Pip

features.name: Sneak Attack (1d6)
features.text: Once per turn, +1d6 damage on a hit with advantage, or when an ally is adjacent to the target.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: Double proficiency on Stealth and Investigation.

pc:pc-3-rogue.backstory: Pip grew up around Shadowdale’s travelers and learned to recognize thieves by their tools, bootwork, and habits. Pip now works with adventurers to prove that sharp eyes and quicker hands can serve people as well as pocket them.

adventure.pitch: A grounded, immediate roadside robbery in Cormyr’s King’s Forest: the party survives an ambush, extracts the truth from a captured bandit, and strikes the nearby camp before the gang can move its stolen goods.

scene:b1.title: Fern-Line Ambush
scene:b1.summary: The scene opens mid-fight. Three weak bandits are already visible and hostile: one rushes from the left fern bank, one advances from the right among the trunks, and one blocks the road ahead with a drawn crossbow. The party has clear ground for movement, with tree trunks and fern patches offering cover. There is no ally, negotiation, clue-solving, or other objective here—only surviving the ambush. The bandits fight to rob the party, not to die needlessly, and one may break if the others fall.

scenePlan.look: A straight, open forest road runs between tall tree trunks, with broad fern banks on both sides and clear packed earth in the center. There is no water, bridge, building, cart, or other structure.
scenePlan.mood: dim amber dusk under a darkening forest canopy
features: dense fern banks on both sides
a leaning alder at the road edge

scene:b2.title: The Survivor Talks
scene:b2.summary: After the ambush, one living bandit is trapped, wounded, or surrendered. Harl Voss admits plainly that the attack was a robbery and gives up the camp’s location: a disused charcoal-burner’s hollow north of the road, marked by alder twigs tied with red thread. The party can question him, threaten him, bargain for his freedom, bind him, or use compassionate treatment; suggested checks include DC 11 Insight to spot lies, DC 12 Intimidation or Persuasion to make him cooperate, and DC 10 Medicine to stabilize him. Harl notices Aldric’s old caravan-guard buckle, while Pip recognizes the crude Shadowdale-style boot stitching on Harl’s footwear. Elara can identify the gang’s lamp oil and determine that the camp is close enough to reach before full dark.

scenePlan.look: A widened bend in the forest road contains trampled ferns, scattered weapons, and a fallen log beside a shallow leaf-covered hollow. Tall trees ring the clearing, with no buildings or water nearby.
scenePlan.mood: blue dusk with the last warm light fading through branches
features: alder-twig marker tied with red thread

scene:b3.title: The Charcoal-Burner’s Hollow
scene:b3.summary: Following Harl’s directions, the party finds the gang’s rough camp before it can relocate. Rusk Vale, the remaining leader, is packing stolen sacks and a locked trade chest while one other bandit watches the road. The party can approach openly, sneak through the trees, lure the guards away, parley, or attack. Rusk offers the goods in exchange for Harl if pressured, but abandons any bargain once escape looks impossible. The red-thread markers and alder twigs confirm Harl’s story; Aldric can identify the trade chest as caravan property, Pip can open it or search the camp, and Elara can safely extinguish the camp’s oil lanterns or use the terrain against the guards.

scenePlan.look: A shallow clearing sits in a bowl of roots and charcoal-black earth. A low canvas lean-to, stacked crates, a cold fire ring, and a narrow trail leading back toward the King’s Road occupy the hollow.
scenePlan.mood: near-night gloom beneath a clouded forest sky

blueprint.premise: A grounded, immediate roadside robbery in Cormyr’s King’s Forest: the party survives an ambush, extracts the truth from a captured bandit, and strikes the nearby camp before the gang can move its stolen goods.
blueprint.centralProblem: Three bandits attack the party on the King’s Road, part of a small gang holding stolen caravan supplies at a fern-hidden camp nearby. The party must survive, learn the camp’s location from the survivor, and recover the goods.
blueprint.intendedEnding: The party reaches the bandit camp, defeats or drives off its leader, secures the stolen caravan goods, and leaves the captured survivor bound for judgment by Cormyr’s Purple Dragons.
blueprint.opening: At dusk on the King’s Road through Cormyr’s King’s Forest, the party is already under attack: three bandits burst from the ferns and close across the open road.

spine.intent: The party defeats or scatters the three attackers and gains control of the roadside.
The survivor identifies the nearby camp and confirms this was a straightforward robbery.
The party secures the stolen goods and defeats or drives off the remaining bandits.
The recovered cargo and any prisoner are carried to Cormyr’s Purple Dragons for judgment.

brief.activeBeatIntent: The ambush is more than a roadside attack: the party must secure a living thread to the hidden camp before the gang realizes its assault failed.

reachable.hook: A surviving bandit, wounded or cornered, may trade the camp’s location and the stolen goods’ whereabouts for mercy or protection.

clocks: The gang’s lookout may discover the ambush has failed and warn the camp.
The stolen caravan goods are being prepared for movement or concealment.
brief.notes: The party has not yet chosen a direction, so the direct path to the survivor remains open; the scene can also reveal signs that make pursuit feel urgent rather than predetermined.

npc:harl-voss.name: Harl Voss
npc:harl-voss.appearance: A lean man in his thirties with a split lower lip, muddy brown leathers, and red thread tied around one wrist.

voice.tic: He rubs the red thread between two fingers whenever he hesitates.
voice.want: To survive questioning and avoid a hanging.
voice.fear: That Rusk will find him before the authorities do.

persona.stake: He will trade the camp’s location for protection and a chance to live.

npc:rusk-vale.name: Rusk Vale
npc:rusk-vale.appearance: A broad, weathered man in his forties wearing a patched green cloak, iron-studded gloves, and a pale scar across his nose.

voice.tic: He calls everyone “traveler” and smiles without warmth before making threats.
voice.want: To escape with the trade chest and rebuild elsewhere.
voice.fear: Being recognized and taken alive by Cormyr’s Purple Dragons.

persona.stake: He will abandon his camp and followers to save himself.

journal.text: The company learned that the caravan had vanished and three robbers had ambushed them along Cormyr’s King’s Forest road.
Aldric drew steel; Fern-Bank was five feet northwest, Trunkside ten feet north, and Roadblock five feet west with a crossbow.

Aldric leads you along the King’s Road, a scarred human fighter who once guarded caravans and still wears a dented buckle from an ambush he survived. Elara travels beside him, a high elf wizard trading Suzail’s lecture halls for practical magic in untamed places. Pip keeps to the roadside, a lightfoot halfling whose sharp eyes learned among Shadowdale’s travelers to read a thief by bootwork and tools. Together, you seek work where caution, terrain, and quick hands matter.

Dusk settles through Cormyr’s King’s Forest as you press onward, the road pale beneath the darkening trees and fern-fronds whispering in the breeze. Then the undergrowth explodes. Three bandits burst from the ferns, boots pounding onto the open road as they close around you, steel flashing in the last red light.
